title: Pipa (four-string lute)
summary: The pipa is a pear-shaped Chinese lute held upright and plucked with the fingers. Four strings run over tall frets, so players can press, slide and bend a note. It is best known for the tremolo, a fast roll of one note that turns a single pluck into a long shimmering line.
howToPlay: The four strings run down the neck, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks the fret where a note is played.
A bead slides down the string to its fret. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
The long lane near the bridge is the tremolo: tap it on the beat and the note rolls on its own.
Try the lyrical line first, then the lively march, then the rolling tremolo.
rules: The notes come from a five-note scale: A, B, C sharp, E and F sharp, in two octaves.
The tremolo lane sounds a rolled note and is scored once, at its start.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The pipa has been played in China for roughly two thousand years and appears in poems, paintings and songs. Makers still shape the pear-shaped body and set the tall frets by hand.
